    Hamiltonian Mechanics very briefly

    Classical Mechanics: Total energy of a system = kinetic energy + potential energy


    The Hamiltonian is a scalar function, H(q,p)H(q, p), that represents the total energy of the system in terms of phase space pairs.
    Hamiltonian Mechanics: describes a system's energy in terms of coordinate phase space pairs.
    Each system has its own function to describe its motion, which is what the HNN attempts to learn.
    p=(p1,...,pN)\textbf{p} = (p_1, ..., p_N) momentum of a set of objects
    q=(q1,...,qN)\textbf{q} = (q_1, ..., q_N) position of a set of objects

    Mass-Spring as simple example

    Conservation of energy leads to symmetry in the systems of motion
    Motion of the Ideal Mass-Spring in one dimension shows reflection symmetry
    Modeled by the equation H(q,p)=12kq2+p22mH(q, p) = \frac{1}{2}kq^2 + \frac{p^2}{2m}
    Simplified for illustration
    spring constant k=2k = 2
    mass constant m=12m = \frac{1}{2}
    H(q,p)=q2+p2H(q, p) = q^2 + p^2

    Ordinary Gradient vs Symplectic Gradient

    For our ideal mass-spring system
    Symplectic Gradient
    • Swap order and negate the second one
    • Now total energy HH does not change
    • Points orthogonally to ∇H\nabla H
    Ordinary Gradient
    ∇H=[∂H∂q,  ∂H∂p]=[2q,  2p]\nabla H = \left[\frac{\partial H}{\partial q},\; \frac{\partial H}{\partial p}\right] = [2q,\; 2p]
    SH=[∂H∂p,  −∂H∂q]=[2p,  −2q]S_H = \left[\frac{\partial H}{\partial p},\; -\frac{\partial H}{\partial q}\right] = [2p,\; -2q]
    • Points "Uphill" toward quickest increase of HH

    Time Derivative Vector Field for the ideal mass-spring
    Larger ∣p∣\lvert p \rvert means moving faster

    Always clockwise rotation because pp > 0 means positive velocity (qq getting larger). Top half.
    When p<0p < 0 is negative velocity (qq getting smaller). Bottom half
    compressed ↔\leftrightarrow stretched
    Vector field shows the symplectic gradient SHS_H

    What is a Hamiltonian Neural Net?

      A HNN learns the scalar energy function from the (q,p)(q, p) pairs
      "Instead of crafting the Hamiltonian by hand, we propose parameterizing it with a
      neural network and then learning it directly from data."

      Taylor

      Architecture

      Always moving along symplectic gradient of H, preserves energy.
      dHθdt=(∂Hθ∂q)(∂Hθ∂p)+(∂Hθ∂p)(−∂Hθ∂q)=0\frac{dH_{\theta}}{dt} = \left(\frac{\partial H_{\theta}}{\partial q}\right)\left(\frac{\partial H_{\theta}}{\partial p}\right) + \left(\frac{\partial H_{\theta}}{\partial p}\right)\left(-\frac{\partial H_{\theta}}{\partial q}\right) = 0

      Backward Pass

      Why tanh instead of ReLU?
      The 2nd derivative of ReLU is 0 almost everywhere. Tanh has a smooth 2nd derivative.
      ∂∂θ(∂Hθ∂q),∂∂θ(∂Hθ∂p)\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \left( \frac{\partial H_\theta}{\partial q} \right) ,\quad \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \left( \frac{\partial H_\theta}{\partial p} \right)
      2nd-order Mixed Partials

      Initialization

      Orthogonal matricies have a magnitude of exactly 1. Signals neither grow nor shrink.
      The linear layers of the baseline MLP are initialized orthogonally.

      for l in [self.linear1, self.linear2, self.linear3]:
      torch.nn.init.orthogonal_(l.weight)
      Inits so that WTW=IW^TW = I
      Ensures uniform gradient flow across layers
      Orthogonal
      Important for tanh 

      Training - What's different?

      Key differences of HNN compared to Baseline MLP
      • System of motion learned from relatively few examples (750 for ideal mass-spring experiment)
      • Uses full batch gradient descent; no mini-batches
      • Tracks gradients for both training and eval modes (requires_grad=True for training and test data)
      • HNN calculates the time derivative and calculates loss for the vector field at every training step
      • therefore, 1 step == 1 epoch

      Training - What's ordinary?

      Some HNN components would be found in any Baseline MLP
      • HNN defines its own L2_loss function, but that's just MSE of the time derivatives
      • Optimizer is Adam with learning rate 1e-3 and weight decay of 1e-4
      • No data augmentation necessary in ideal mass-spring example
